facts.statement: The type specimen of Skorpiovenator was formally described in 2009 and is considered one of the most complete abelisaurid skeletons known.
facts.quote: Formally described in 2009, the type specimen is one of the most complete and informative abelisaurids yet known, described from a nearly complete and articulated skeleton.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Skorpiovenator bustingorryi was discovered in 2005 by paleontologists Juan Ignacio Canale and Agustín Scanferla.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Skorpiovenator bustingorryi (MMCH-PV 48K) was discovered in 2005 by Juan Ignacio Canale and Agustín Scanferla.

facts.statement: The genus name Skorpiovenator means "scorpion hunter" in Latin, referencing the predator's nature and the abundance of scorpions found at the excavation site.
facts.quote: The generic name derives from the Latin words skorpios ("scorpion") and venator ("hunter"), referring to its nature as a predator and the abundance of scorpions at the dig site.

facts.statement: The species name bustingorryi honors Manuel Bustingorry, the farm owner who died before the species was formally described.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Manuel Bustingorry, who had died by the time the paper was released.

facts.statement: The description of Skorpiovenator led researchers to establish a new abelisaurid clade called Brachyrostra.
facts.quote: In naming Skorpiovenator, Canale and colleagues erected a new abelisaurid clade, Brachyrostra, to which it was assigned.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator was an abelisaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Early Cretaceous (Albian) period.
facts.quote: Skorpiovenator ("scorpion hunter") is a genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) Huincul Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: The fossil strata containing the type specimen are now dated to the late Albian stage, approximately 106.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: The strata from which MMCH-PV 48K was recovered belong to the lower part of the Huincul Formation in Patagonia, which was originally dated to the late Cenomanian stage, about 95 million years ago, though is now dated to the late Albian, about 106.2 million years ago.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator was classified as a fairly large abelisaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Skorpiovenator was a fairly large abelisaurid.

facts.statement: The preserved portion of the type specimen measures 4.35 meters in length.
facts.quote: What is preserved of the type specimen measures 4.35 m in length.

facts.statement: Based on the anatomy of related species, Skorpiovenator is estimated to have reached a length of 6 to 6.2 meters and a weight of slightly under 900 kilograms.
facts.quote: Based on the anatomy of close relatives, it may have been between 6 - 6.2 m long in life, and may have weighed a little under 900 kg.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator had a short, blunt skull that resembled that of Carnotaurus.
facts.quote: Its skull was short and blunt, and somewhat resembled that of Carnotaurus.

facts.statement: The rugose bone texture of Skorpiovenator suggests the presence of large facial scales.
facts.quote: Its bone texture was rugose, even by the standards of other abelisaurids, which indicates the presence of large facial scales.

facts.statement: Small pits called foramina on the skull suggest that Skorpiovenator had a high degree of facial sensitivity.
facts.quote: The skull is also covered in small pits called foramina, which suggests a strong degree of facial sensitivity.

facts.statement: The excavated skeleton measures 4.35 meters from the premaxilla to the 12th tail vertebra.
facts.quote: The preserved length of the excavated Skorpiovenator skeleton, measured from the premaxilla to the 12th caudal (tail) vertebra is 4.35 m.

facts.statement: Because most of the tail is missing, the maximum estimated length is 6 to 6.2 meters and the maximum estimated weight is 891 kilograms.
facts.quote: Since it lacks most of the tail, precise length measurements are currently impossible, but it has been estimated to have grown up to 6 - 6.2 m long and weighed up to 891 kg.

facts.statement: A fragment of the right tibia was assigned to Skorpiovenator in 2022.
facts.quote: In 2022, the proximal (far) end of a right tibia, MMCh-PV255, was assigned to Skorpiovenator.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator had a skull measuring 54.1 cm in length from the premaxilla to the quadrate.
facts.quote: The skull of Skorpiovenator, measured from the premaxilla to the quadrate, measured 54.1 cm in length.

facts.statement: The postorbital bone of Skorpiovenator was large and intersected the eye socket, nearly touching the opposite lacrimal bone.
facts.quote: The postorbital was large, and intersected the orbit (eye socket), to the point where it almost contacted the lacrimal on the opposite side.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator had four teeth in each premaxilla and 19 teeth in each maxilla, a count higher than in any other abelisaurid.
facts.quote: Each of Skorpiovenator's premaxillae bore four teeth, whereas each maxilla bore 19 teeth, more than in any other abelisaurid.

facts.statement: Based on a preserved skeleton length of 4.37 meters, Skorpiovenator is estimated to have reached about 6 meters in total length.
facts.quote: Se estima que el Skorpiovenator llegaba a medir unos 6 m de longitud, con base en su esqueleto con una longitud preservada de 4,37 m.

facts.statement: Although Skorpiovenator's arms and scapulae were not found, they are assumed to have been short like in related species.
facts.quote: Ni sus brazos ni sus escápulas fueron hallados, pero se supone que eran cortos como en especies afines

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator's thin jaws held several sharp teeth with serrated edges.
facts.quote: Sus mandíbulas delgadas poseían varios dientes afilados con bordes aserrados.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Skorpiovenator may have used its high skull like a mace, swinging it backward against prey so its teeth could penetrate with enough force to cause damage.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio puede haber usado su cráneo alto como un mazo, llevando la cabeza hacia atrás y aventándola contra su presa de manera que sus dientes penetraran con la fuerza suficiente como para provocar daño a la presa.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (MMCH-PV 48) of Skorpiovenator is housed in the Municipal Museum "Ernesto Bachmann" in Villa El Chocón, Neuquén, Argentina.
facts.quote: El holotipo (MMCH-PV 48) se encuentra en el Museo Municipal "Ernesto Bachmann", de Villa El Chocón, Neuquén, Argentina.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator was formally described and named by Canale, Scanferla, Agnolin, and Novas in 2009, though the description article was digitally pre-published in 2008.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo fue descrito y nombrado por Canale, Scanferla, Agnolin y Novas en 2009, si bien el artículo de descripción fue prepublicado digitalmente en 2008.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 95 and 93 million years ago, in the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior, entre 95 a 93 millones de años, durante el Cenomaniano

facts.statement: Fossils of Skorpiovenator were found in the Huincul Formation in Neuquén, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles fueron encontrados en la Formación Huincul en Neuquén, de la Patagonia argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Skorpiovenator was established by Canale et al. in 2008.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Canale et al., 2008

facts.statement: The species Skorpiovenator bustingorryi was described by Canale et al. in 2008.
facts.quote: species_authority: Canale et al., 2008

facts.statement: In 2009, Canale et al. placed Skorpiovenator within the subclade Brachyrostra, a group of short-snouted Carnotaurinae.
facts.quote: In 2009, Canale et al. published a phylogenetic analysis focusing on the South American carnotaurines. In their results, they found that all South American forms (including Skorpiovenator) grouped together as a sub-clade of Carnotaurinae, which they named Brachyrostra, meaning "short snouts".

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation, where Skorpiovenator fossils are found, is estimated to be 106.2 million years old.
facts.quote: The age of this formation is estimated at 106.2 million years ago.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator shared its Late Cretaceous habitat with giant sauropods like Argentinosaurus and other dinosaurs such as Choconsaurus and Chucarosaurus.
facts.quote: Skorpiovenator shared its environment with the sauropods Argentinosaurus (one of the largest sauropods, if not the largest), Choconsaurus, Chucarosaurus and Cathartesaura.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator likely lived at the same time as other carnivores including the carcharodontosaurid Mapusaurus and the abelisaurid Ilokelesia.
facts.quote: Puede haber vivido en la misma época que otros carnívoros, como el carcarodontosáurido Mapusaurus y otro abelisáurido, Ilokelesia.

facts.statement: The species name honors Manuel Bustingorry, the owner of the field where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie Skorpiovenator bustingorryi es en honor a Manuel Bustingorry, dueño del campo donde fue encontrado.

facts.statement: The name also references the large number of scorpions present at the excavation site.
facts.quote: Además, el nombre también hace referencia a la gran cantidad de escorpiones que había en el sitio de excavación.

facts.statement: The clade Brachyrostra is defined as all abelisaurids more closely related to Carnotaurus sastrei than to Majungasaurus crenatissimus.
facts.quote: Por definición, el clado comprende a "todos los abelisáuridos más cercanamente relacionados con Carnotaurus sastrei que con Majungasaurus crenatissimus."

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that isolated teeth previously assigned to Carcharodontosauridae actually belong to abelisaurids based on similarities with Skorpiovenator's teeth.
facts.quote: Basándose en la similitudes entre los dientes de Skorpiovenator y los carcarodontosáuridos, los autores mencionados sugieren que los dientes aislados encontrados de edad posteriore al Cenomaniano y antes asignados a la familia Carcharodontosauridae de manera indeterminada, pertenecerían en realidad a abelisáuridos.

facts.statement: Skorpiovenator lived during the Albian stage, between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Skorpiovenator in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2

facts.statement: A description of the skull anatomy of Skorpiovenator bustingorryi was published by Canale et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: Description of the anatomy of the skull of Skorpiovenator bustingorryi is published by Canale et al. (2026).

rejected.statement: Skorpiovenator lived in an arid environment with ephemeral or seasonal streams during the Late Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: The Huincul Formation, from which Skorpiovenator is known, is thought to represent an arid environment with ephemeral or seasonal streams.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'an arid environment with ephemeral or seasonal streams'

rejected.statement: Canale et al. (2008) grouped Skorpiovenator with other South American forms into a subclade called Brachyrostra, meaning "short snout".
rejected.quote: En sus resultados, hallaron que todas las formas sudamericanas (incluyendo a Skorpiovenator) se agrupan en un subgrupo de la subfamilia Carnotaurinae, al cual denominaron Brachyrostra, que significa "rostro corto".
